THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:27.02.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.643/2014 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & JMFC, M.A.C.T., GUBBI,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSTION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The owner of the offending vehicle as well as the claimant are in appeal.
2. It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle which was owned by The Priya English School was not insured, and therefore, it would be liable to pay the compensation.
3. The Tribunal, on analysis of the evidence adduced before it, has awarded Rs.9,50,000/-.
In order to come to this conclusion the Tribunal has assessed the disability to the whole body at 20% and has assessed the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.10,500/-.

The evidence on record indicates that the Doctor who treated the claimant has stated that the claimant has suffered 79% disability to the left lower limb and 40.6% to the left upper limb and as a consequence he had suffered permanent disability at 36.45% to the whole body.
4. In my view, in the light of the clear evidence, the Tribunal could not have reduced the disability of claimant from 36.45% to 20%.
The compensation of the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.10,500/- cannot be found fault with since it was supported by the say of the employer.

As a consequence, towards 'loss of future earning' the claimant would be entitled for Rs.8,26,686/-
(Rs.10,500/- x 12 x 18 x 36.45%).
The award by the Tribunal in respect of other heads are just and proper and do not call for interference.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to the following sums :
Sl. Amount  Particulars No. in (Rs.)
 1. Medical expenses 3,56,400/-
 2. Pain and sufferings 50,000/-
 3. Nourishment and diet food 10,000/-
 4. Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 5. Loss of future earnings 8,26,686/-
 6.

Future medical expenses 50,000/-
Halesha vs Panchakshari on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58110258/
The appeal of the owner of the vehicle is dismissed.
The appeal of the claimant is allowed in part.

6. Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.13,23,086/- as against Rs.9,50,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
7. The owner of offending vehicle is directed to deposit the deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

8. Out of the award amount, 60% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of five years in any Nationalised Bank in the name of claimant and remaining 40% of the award amount shall be released in favour of claimant after the deposit made by the owner of offending vehicle.

Sd/-
